patch_description: Instead of symmetry-constrained pattern search, this uses a fundamentally different paradigm: time-budgeted simulated annealing over all 26 coordinates with three move classes — (1) single-point perturbations, (2) small random affine (linear) transformations of the whole configuration (stretch/shear — which genuinely change the min-triangle/hull-area ratio and can escape local optima unreachable by single-point moves), and (3) global scaling about the centroid. All moves are accepted/rejected on the exact true score (min triangle area / hull area). After each annealing run, a short greedy coordinate polish converges to a sharp local optimum. Multiple deterministic seeds (3-fold symmetric, lattice, and random) are annealed within a fixed wall-clock budget, and the best configuration across all runs is returned. Annealing with affine moves explores the ratio landscape far more broadly than hill-climbing on a 4-point symmetric parametrization, which previously got stuck in symmetric basins.
